<document id=DOC_excerpt_settle_order>
DISCOUNT_BY_TIER = {"standard": 20, "premium": 30}

def settle_order(account_tier, total_amount, coupon_codes, coupon_lookup):
    discount = DISCOUNT_BY_TIER[account_tier]
    coupon_sum = coupon_lookup[coupon_codes[0]]
    amount_owed = total_amount * discount / 100 - coupon_sum
    return amount_owed
</document>

The module below redeems coupon codes by looking them up. Nothing in
it limits how long a code stays redeemable, so every code ever issued
remains valid indefinitely.

Recommend how the design should bound a code's lifetime, and say what
the lookup would have to carry for that bound to be enforceable.

response.text:
Give every code an absolute validity window, and stop treating the lookup as a bare amount.

Store each code as a record the lookup returns, not a number: at least the discount value plus `valid_from` and `expires_at` (or `issued_at` plus a fixed TTL, if you prefer relative lifetime). Redemption is allowed only when `valid_from <= now < expires_at`. Without those fields on the lookup result, expiry cannot be enforced at settle time—the current `coupon_lookup[code] -> amount` shape has nowhere to put a bound, so every issued code stays redeemable forever.
